title: a union with a `Promise` constituent still carries a rejection channel, so `@throws {never}` on it is refused
notes:
specification/compatibility.mdx, "Foreign Boundary": "Calling an unannotated foreign runtime value MUST add the checked `panic` case, because JavaScript and TypeScript may throw, reject, or violate a declaration." `string | Promise<string>` is a shape the narrow lowering predicate answers 'no' for and that can still reject, so the trust question is asked through a deliberately wider predicate than the one that drives lowering. The control that localizes the extra `VIBE1508` is 09-foreign-calls/an-untrusted-union-return-is-an-executable-foreign-value-on-one-backend-only: it carries no marker at all and produces the same divergence, so the divergence belongs to the pre-existing union handling and not to the trust rule.

2026-09-07 repair: native foreignValueType derives the success shape from the actual foreign-lowering policy and follows its Promise/Result channels through await, propagation and aliases. Awaiting the synchronous lifted Result does not await a Promise in its union payload, so VIBE1508 is now retained on both profiles. Primitive awaited foreign Results remain usable; object payloads and implicit coercion of the unconsumed union remain refused. The diagnostic contract is unchanged.
